topics.name: Selecting and safely operating commercial kitchen equipment
topics.rationale: Nine of the thirteen units carry a knowledge point reading safe operational practices using essential functions and features of equipment, and six carry an element about using equipment to prepare food. SITHCCC023 Use food preparation equipment is delivered second, before every cookery unit, and it is the unit whose whole subject this is.
topics.teachingRule: Each later cookery unit restates in a line or two the equipment its own dishes need and any setting peculiar to them, prompts the learner to name the checks they would make before use, then teaches that equipment in full. It does not re-explain assembly, safe operation or the manufacturer instruction from scratch. Its tool still evidences the equipment requirement in full - applied, inside a question about its own dishes or carried by an observation item, against the owner's benchmark. SITXFSA006 is not a recaller of this topic: it teaches its own small equipment requirement in full - calibrating, using, cleaning and fault-checking a temperature probe, and choosing cleaning and sanitising equipment and materials to manufacturer advice - and is assessed on those.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer selects the equipment for the task, states the pre-use check and the manufacturer instruction that governs its safe operation, and describes assembly, safe use, shutdown and cleaning. It states what makes the equipment unsafe to use and what is done then.

topics.name: Mise en place: what it means and why it governs the kitchen
topics.rationale: The meaning and role of mise en place is stated in three units. It belongs where a learner first organises a workstation, which is SITHCCC023 in week two.
topics.teachingRule: SITHCCC025 and SITHCCC027 plan their own mise en place and are assessed on the plan working, not on defining the term.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer defines mise en place as everything prepared and positioned before service so the cook works without interruption, and gives the consequence of poor mise en place on quality, timing and safety during service.

topics.name: Keeping food safe and saleable in storage: date codes, rotation, storage conditions, shelf life and freshness
topics.rationale: Four families - date codes and rotation labels in six units, environmental storage conditions in five, optimising shelf life in five, and freshness and quality indicators in four - are one topic, and it is the subject of SITXINV006 Receive, store and maintain stock, delivered fourth. Twenty restatements of how to store food across a thirteen-unit certificate.
topics.teachingRule: A cookery unit states only what is SPECIFIC to its own commodity - that a dressed salad holds badly, that a filled sandwich is a potentially hazardous food - and cites SITXINV006 for the storage system, the rotation method and the labelling.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer reads a date code, applies stock rotation so oldest saleable stock is used first, states the storage condition the item requires - temperature, humidity, covering, separation from raw - and names the freshness indicators that decide whether it is used or discarded.

topics.name: Work health and safety: legislation, duties and the consequences of failure
topics.rationale: Three families - the ramifications of failing to observe legislation, employee responsibilities, and safe work practices for a job role - are one body of law and duty. SITXWHS005 Participate in safe work practices is delivered first, in week one.
topics.teachingRule: The food safety units cite SITXWHS005 for the structure of duty, breach and penalty, and name the Food Act as their own instrument.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states the duty the WHS Act places on the employer and on the worker, identifies the hazards of the kitchen and the control for each, and names the consequence of failure for the worker, the business and the individual - including prosecution and penalty.

topics.name: Food safety law, the Food Standards Code and the meaning of contamination
topics.rationale: One account of the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code, of what a contaminant and a potentially hazardous food are, and of the regulator. Three units carry it; SITXFSA005 is delivered third and is where it belongs.
topics.teachingRule: SITXINV006 and SITXFSA006 name the specific requirement governing their activity - a temperature, a record, a disposal rule - and cite the Code clause rather than re-summarising the Code.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer defines a contaminant, contamination and a potentially hazardous food in the terms the Food Standards Code uses, names the Code and the state Food Act as the instruments, and states the role of the local enforcement agency.

topics.name: Safe handling of different food types
topics.rationale: SITHCCC023 is delivered second and SITXFSA006 seventh, so the equipment unit meets food-type handling first - it cannot teach a learner to use a slicer on cooked meat without saying how that meat is handled. SITXFSA006 Participate in safe food handling practices then covers the full matrix. OWNERSHIP CORRECTED 9 September 2026: the previous rationale claimed SITHCCC023 is delivered second and SITXFSA006 seventh. The course record says the reverse - SITXFSA006 is sequence 4 and SITHCCC023 sequence 5 - so SITXFSA006 meets the food types first and owns them. SITHCCC023 names only the handling point peculiar to the equipment in front of the learner - how cooked meat is handled at the slicer, how raw egg is handled at the mixer - and cites SITXFSA006 for the rest.
topics.teachingRule: SITHCCC023 introduces handling only as far as its own equipment demands. SITXFSA006 teaches the DELTA and it is substantial: every high-risk food type, cross-contamination between them, and the temperature control each requires.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states the handling requirement for each high-risk food type - dairy, eggs, meat, poultry, seafood, smallgoods, prepared fruit and vegetables - the temperature control each needs, and the cross-contamination risk between them.

topics.name: Cleaning products, chemicals and their safe use
topics.rationale: SITXFSA005 is delivered third and SITHKOP009 sixth. SITXFSA005 cannot explain why a surface must be sanitised without naming what sanitises it, and a learner cannot recall a chemical they have not met.
topics.teachingRule: SITXFSA005 introduces sanitising at the level food safety requires. SITHKOP009 Clean kitchen premises and equipment teaches the DELTA - the product range, dilution ratios, chemical storage, the PPE each demands, and reading a safety data sheet.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states why a surface must be cleaned and then sanitised, selects the product for the surface, and states the dilution, contact time and PPE the product requires and where it is stored.

unownedTopicsNote: A requirement not appearing here overlapped nothing: it is unique to its unit, that unit teaches it, and no ruling was needed.
assessmentNote: ASSESSMENT IS PER UNIT. A ruling never removes a requirement from an applying unit's assessment tool - every unit is separately certified and evidences its own requirements in full, on its own mapped line, with no line naming another unit as its evidence. assessmentDepth governs DEPTH and FORM only: "applied" means assessed inside a question about this unit's own subject or carried by an observation item, against the owner's benchmark; "full" means this unit teaches and assesses its own subject matter in full. The register exists to keep those benchmarks consistent across the units that share a requirement, which is what Standard 1.5 validation tests.
